'''Horst Stöcker''' (born 1952) is a German [[theoretical physicist]] and Judah M. Eisenberg Professor Laureatus at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] working in [[nuclear physics]] and [[astrophysics]].

==Education and career==
After ''Abitur'' 1971,<ref name=Hoff>{{cite web | last1=Hasani | first1=Ilire | last2=Hoffmann | first2=Robert | title=Academy of Europe: CV | website=Academy of Europe | url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Stöcker_Horst/CV | access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> Stöcker studied physics, chemistry, mathematics and philosophy at the Goethe University Frankfurt, where he got his Dr. phil.nat. in 1979 under [[Walter Greiner]].<ref name=FIAS>{{cite web | title=Horst Stöcker | website=www.fias.science | url=https://www.fias.science/de/theoretische-naturwissenschaften/gruppen/horst-stoecker/ | language=de | access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref> The title of the dissertation was ''Shock waves in nuclear matter – proof by circumstantial evidence''.<ref>{{cite thesis | last=Stöcker | first=Horst | title=Shock waves in nuclear matter : proof by circumstantial evidence | publisher=Universitätsbibliothek Johann Christian Senckenberg | date=1979 | url=https://publikationen.ub.uni-frankfurt.de/frontdoor/index/index/year/2006/docId/2653 | access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

He went on to [[GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research]] and – as a DAAD – postdoctoral fellow – to [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], [[UC Berkeley]].<ref name=FIAS/>

Stöcker joined the faculty of physics and astronomy at [[Michigan State University]] and the National Superconducting Cyclotron Laboratory, NSCL, in 1982.<ref name=FIAS/>

In 1985, Stöcker moved on to a professorship for [[Theoretical Physics]] and [[Astrophysics]] at Goethe University Frankfurt, where Stöcker holds the Judah M. Eisenberg endowed chair since 2004.<ref name=FIAS/>

From 2000 to 2003, Stöcker was twice elected vice president at Goethe University, for science, mathematics, computer science, IT and high performance computing, HPC, for the medical school and for the {{ill|Universitätsklinikum Frankfurt|de}}, the hospital of the Goethe University.<ref name=Hoff/> He was re-elected ViP for a third time 2006–2007.<ref name=Hoff/>

Stöcker is senior fellow, and, with Walter Greiner and [[Wolf Singer]], founding director and chair of the executive board at the international interdisciplinary [[Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies]] (FIAS) – a public-private scientific foundation for theoretical research in fundamental science, natural science and computational life science, of Goethe University.<ref name=FIAS/><ref name="FAZ l437">{{cite news | last=Rauchhaupt | first=Ulf von | title=Ein Wissenschaftsmanager mit entwaffnendem Humor | website=FAZ.NET | date=16 December 2022 | url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/wissen/physik-mehr/ein-wissenschaftsmanager-mit-entwaffnendem-humor-18537852.html | language=de | access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

Horst Stöcker was the scientific chairman and CEO (director general) at the Darmstadt GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research, 2007–2015.<ref>[http://www.gsi.de/organisation/organigramm_e.html Organization overview]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101228054359/http://www.gsi.de/organisation/organigramm_e.html |date=December 28, 2010 }}</ref><ref name="FAZ l437" />

In 2008 Stöcker was elected vice-president of {{ill|Helmholtz Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren HGF|de}} for the Research Area "Struktur der Materie", 2008, and was reelected 2010–2012.<ref name=Hoff/>

==Honors==
* ''{{ill|Judah Moshe Eisenberg|de}} Professor Laureatus für Theoretische Physik'', at Goethe University Frankfurt<ref name=Hoff/>
* Doctor honoris causa of the Russian Academy of Sciences, RAS, Moscow, Russia
* Doctor honoris causa of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna, Russia
* Doktor honoris causa of the University of Bucharest, Romania
* Fellow of the European Physical Society, EPS, London, Great Britain
* Fellow of the Institute of Physics, IoP, London, Great Britain
* Member, Deutsche Akademie der Technikwissenschaften, [[acatech]], Munich<ref name=FIAS/>
* Member, [[Academia Europaea]], London, Great Britain<ref name=Hoff/>
* [[Hessian Order of Merit]]<ref name=FIAS/>

Stöcker published around 500 publications that were cited around 50,000 times, supervised around 50 doctoral students, and submitted 5 patents.<ref name=FIAS/>
<!--Horst Stöcker was a guest professor at various distinct Universities and member of Scientific Councils at numerous Institutes worldwide, including the [[US Department of Energy]], [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]], and [[University of California]] in United States; [[Riken]] and [[J-PARC]] in Japan; [[University of Science and Technology of China]] in China; [[CNRS]], [[Université Louis Pasteur]], [[Université de Nantes]], [[GANIL]], and [[Caen]] in France; and [[Tel Aviv University]] in Israel.-->
